---

# WalkMe — 2025-2026 Marketing Narrative Research

## Name / What-it-is / URL
**WalkMe** (now **SAP WalkMe**, acquired by SAP for ~$1.5B, completed Sept 2024). A Digital Adoption Platform (DAP): an overlay layer that sits on top of every app in the enterprise stack, detects where users hit friction, and delivers in-context guidance and automation.
URL: https://www.walkme.com/

---

## VERBATIM Taglines & Hero Copy (walkme.com homepage)

- **"WalkMe turns AI potential into AI performance."** (main hero)
- **"The context your AI is missing."**
- **"AI that follows the work."**
- **"From answers to execution."**
- **"Wherever work happens, it is already there."**
- **"This is what AI was supposed to feel like."**
- **"WalkMe is the critical layer that makes enterprise AI work. It overlays every application, giving AI the real-time context, cross-application reach, and workflow execution it needs to deliver results."**
- **"AI reads the screen and understands what needs to happen next."**
- **"AI handles the full workflow. It knows the next step and takes it."**

Product-page copy (walkme.com/product):
- **"WalkMe AI: Omnipresent contextual AI assistance"**
- **"Create personalized user experiences that guarantee users quickly onboard"**

The flagship 2026 event tagline: **"AI adoption that actually works. Not as a pilot program, but at enterprise scale, across your entire workforce."**

---

## The STORY FRAME — how they narrate walking an employee through a system/change

The dominant 2026 frame is **"What If Work Just Knew?"** — the software anticipates the moment and surfaces help without the employee asking. From the Q2 2026 release (walkme.com/blog/q2-26-release):

- **"Contextual guidance that appears at the right moment, in the right application, without switching tabs or asking for help."**
- **"You're working in the CRM. You hover over a field. And instead of opening a new tab, switching to another app, or pinging a colleague, the context you need just appears."**
- **"AI Chat works the same way, reading what's actually on your screen to give you answers that fit your situation, not a generic help article."**
- **"When technology is working, it fades into the background. What stays is the work getting done."**

The narrative is explicitly **anti-tutorial**. It is not "here is a course, walk through these steps." It is: the system silently reads your screen and injects the exact next action in the flow. The "walking through" is done *by the software, invisibly*, not narrated as a guided journey the employee consciously travels.

Legacy DAP frame (still present via SAP): guidance is delivered **"right in the flow of work"** — the platform **"detects where people encounter friction and provides the tailored support and automation they need to complete the job to be done."**

---

## Emotional / Strategic Angle

The emotional pitch is **relief from software friction and AI disappointment**. Quantified pain drives it:
- **"Employees lose 51 workdays a year to software and AI friction, and organizations capture only 55% of the potential value."**
- **"Seventy-seven percent of workers gave up on their company's AI tools last month and went back to working manually."** (WalkMe data, via Forbes)
- **"When you lose 51 days a year per employee to friction, you do not have a productivity problem, you have a design problem."**

Strategic angle: WalkMe reframes itself from "adoption/training tool" to **"the critical layer that makes enterprise AI work."** The AI-hype pivot is explicit — the value prop is no longer "help users click buttons," it is "give AI the context it lacks so AI actually performs." Emotionally: *"This is what AI was supposed to feel like."*

---

## WHO the buyer is (role-targeting)

WalkMe segments by function on the homepage: **IT, Sales, HR, Customer Care, Public sector** (e.g. "IT — License optimization, AI adoption analytics"; "HR — Onboarding, compliance training, benefits enrollment").

The sharpest **role-targeting language in 2026 aims squarely at the CHRO** (WalkMe-sourced Forbes piece):
- **"The most important seat in the AI economy right now is not the CEO, the CIO, or the Chief AI Officer. It may be the CHRO."**
- **"Fifty-four percent of executives now say adoption is their number one AI challenge."**
- Trust-gap framing: **"Sixty-one percent of executives trust AI to make operational decisions. Only nine percent of workers trust AI for high-impact work."**

On the SAP side the buyer is the **transformation/change owner (CIO + SI-led change management)**: SAP notes strong "attach rates with systems integrators … using the company's technology for change management," and that "SAP leverages WalkMe internally for change management and training."

---

## CRITICAL — AI agent / companion / personalized / 1:1 / in-the-flow language (verbatim)

- **"AI that follows the work."**
- **"Omnipresent contextual AI assistance"** / **"Contextual AI Assistance"** (the named Q2 2026 capability)
- **"the personalized guidance and automation needed to get the job done, right in the flow of work"**
- **"provides the tailored support and automation they need to complete the job to be done"**
- **"reading what's actually on your screen to give you answers that fit your situation"**
- **"AI handles the full workflow. It knows the next step and takes it."**

**SAP / Joule framing (verbatim):**
- **"Integrating the strength of WalkMe's adoption capabilities with SAP's copilot Joule will boost AI assistant and productivity gains."**
- WalkMe is positioned to power **"Joule everywhere"** — extending SAP's Joule generative-AI assistant across SAP *and non-SAP* applications.
- **"pioneered DAP innovations and solutions so companies can effectively navigate the constant change brought on by technology."**

---

## Do they frame a PERSONAL 1:1 AI companion that walks each individual employee through a change?

**Partially — but not in your product's shape.** This is the key competitive finding.

- WalkMe uses **"personalized," "tailored," "contextual," "your situation," "your screen"** heavily, and its AI *is* per-user and per-moment. So there is a personalization claim.
- **BUT the frame is ambient/omnipresent, not a companion relationship.** It is **"Omnipresent contextual AI assistance"** and **"the context just appears"** — an invisible layer that reads your screen, not a named entity/persona that the employee builds a relationship with over time. Their own aesthetic is *"When technology is working, it fades into the background."* WalkMe wants to **disappear**, not to be a companion you talk to.
- Notably, the CHRO-facing article **explicitly rejects the personal-companion path** in favor of role playbooks and peer learning: *"Workers learn AI from the colleague two desks over far faster than from any course."* That is a *human* peer, not a personal AI companion.

**Bottom line for positioning against WalkMe:** WalkMe owns "the invisible context layer that makes enterprise AI work, in the flow of work." They do **not** own — and their brand philosophy actively avoids — the **named, persistent, personal 1:1 AI companion who accompanies one individual employee through a change and builds shared context over time.** That relational/companion framing is white space WalkMe is not claiming.
